summary: Joined node1, node2, node3 into a 3-node RabbitMQ 3.10.0 cluster (Erlang 23.3.4.11, installed via official packagecloud repos on RHEL7), created the `payments` virtual host, and created `app_user` (password generated on-node via openssl, tags=none for least-privilege AMQP-only access) with full configure/write/read permissions on `payments`. Created a durable quorum queue `orders` replicated across all three nodes. Demonstrated message survival: published a persistent message, stopped the queue leader (node1), confirmed leadership failover to node2 and the message remained available, consumed it successfully from node2 while node1 was down, then restored node1 and confirmed full cluster recovery. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id + service-active baselines on all 3 nodes, then sequentially rebooted node1, node2, and node3 (one at a time, waiting for full cluster health/quorum before proceeding to the next), verifying a changed boot_id and full RabbitMQ cluster rejoin + quorum queue integrity after each. Final end-to-end publish (node1)/consume (node3) test after all restarts succeeded, and app_user's tags were reverted to `none` for production use.
actions_performed: Installed Erlang 23.3.4.11 and RabbitMQ 3.10.0 on node1, node2, node3 via packagecloud repos
Opened firewalld ports 4369, 25672, 5672, 15672, 35672-35682 on all nodes
Synchronized Erlang cookie from node1 to node2/node3 via secret_env
Started rabbitmq-server on all nodes and joined node2/node3 to node1's cluster (rabbitmqctl join_cluster)
Generated a random password on node1 and created 'app_user' with full permissions on 'payments', tags=none
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin on node1/node2/node3 for HTTP-API-based publish/consume testing
Declared durable quorum queue 'orders' in 'payments' (replicated across all 3 nodes)

Published a persistent test message, stopped rabbitmq-server on the queue leader (node1), verified leadership failover to node2 and message availability, consumed the message from node2, then restarted node1 and confirmed full cluster rejoin
Captured boot_id and service-health baseline on all 3 nodes

Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 (systemctl reboot), polling each until reachable, verifying changed boot_id, and confirming full RabbitMQ cluster membership + quorum queue health before proceeding to the next node
Ran a final post-restart publish (node1) / consume (node3) test to confirm end-to-end functionality
Reverted app_user tags to 'none' for least-privilege production use

evidence.requirement: message survives loss of one node and remains consumable from remaining nodes
